column1: # Paths ploaness manages in a consumer working tree, because tools ploaness does not run read them from
# there: git, editors, and coding agents cannot resolve a config through node_modules.
#   PINNED    ploaness owns the content; the file must exist and match byte for byte.
#   SEED      ploaness writes it once when absent; the project owns it afterwards.
#   FORBIDDEN the path must not exist, because ploaness supplies that configuration itself.
#   SECTION   ploaness owns the marked block at the top; the project owns the text below it.
#   REFERENCE the path need not exist; if it does it carries nothing but a pointer at AGENTS.md.
# The third column says WHERE the path lives, which a repository holding more than one package has to
# state rather than assume:
#   REPOSITORY  the tree root only. Git, an editor and a coding agent read from there, and one contract
#               per repository is the point - a second copy inside a package would be a second answer.
#   APPLICATION each member that serves one. The sweeps interrogate a running server, so two
#               applications are two sets of answers rather than one shared file.
#   PAYLOAD     each member that can answer at all. Only Payload serves /api/access.
#   EVERYWHERE  the root and every member. A forbidden path shadows what ploaness supplies wherever it
#               sits, so it must not exist in either half.
# Project documentation belongs to the consuming project. The governing standard and the agent guide are
# the exceptions, because together they declare the contract every agent is held to. CLAUDE.md is a fixed
# tool entry point, and AGENTS.md carries the block that points at all three.
README-guideline-software-project.adoc
.ploaness/agent-guide.md
AGENTS.md
CLAUDE.md
.editorconfig
.gitattributes
.nvmrc
.npmrc
# Docker sends the whole directory to the daemon before it reads the first instruction, so what is left
# out is decided here or not at all. The entry that matters is `.env`: the stock Payload Dockerfile does
# `COPY . .` in its builder stage, so an env file in the context lands in that layer and stays in the
# build cache. PINNED rather than SEED for that reason - a project that quietly drops that line puts
# secrets in a layer, and nothing downstream would report it.
.dockerignore
.gitignore
# The three entries below are executable specs rather than configurations. Each judges something only a
# running application knows, and each is PINNED for the reason every other rule belongs to the harness:
# a check the project can edit is not a rule.
# Static rules cannot see a contrast defect that appears only under :hover or :focus, nor a page nobody
# remembered to add to a scan list, so this one crawls instead of reading.
tests/e2e/a11y.e2e.spec.ts
# A Next.js application serves no security header unless the project sets one, and every static gate
# stays green while it does not: the page renders and the build passes. Only the running application
# knows what it sends, so this asks it.
tests/e2e/security-headers.e2e.spec.ts
# The static rules can see that a project decided each operation, and can see an inline always-true
# rule. They cannot see what `read: anyone` decides, nor what Payload made of the config after
# sanitisation, so a project can satisfy every one of them and still serve every document to every
# stranger. Payload reports its own verdict at /api/access; this asks for it with no credential.
tests/e2e/access-boundary.e2e.spec.ts
# The entry-point file a coding agent other than Claude reads. None is required - a project that uses
# only one agent carries only its file - but one that exists carries nothing but a pointer at AGENTS.md.
# The standard puts the rules in the root instruction file and lets a tool-specific one only reference
# it, so two agents working the same repository cannot be answering to two different contracts.
GEMINI.md
.cursorrules
.windsurfrules
.clinerules
.github/copilot-instructions.md
.stylelintrc.json
.dependency-cruiser.json
knip.json
.gitleaks.toml
plugins
